::: {.country-policy-matrix}
### Radical-cure treatment by G6PD status

| G6PD category | Radical-cure treatment policy | Treatment implementation | Implementation details | Health-system level | Health-system details | Implementation year | Additional safety recommendations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G6PD normal: ≥ 6.1 Ul/gHb** | TQ 300 mg or 100mg, 200 mg | Implemented | No primaquine or tafenoquine without G6PD testing | Up to community level | Up to community malaria unit level | 2024 | Not specified |
| **G6PD intermediate: 4.1-6.0 Ul/gHb** | PQ 0.5 mg/kg/day over 7 days | Implemented | No primaquine or tafenoquine without G6PD testing | Up to community level | Up to community malaria unit level | 2024 | Not specified |
| **G6PD deficient: ≤ 4.0 Ul/gHb** | PQ 0.75 mg/kg/week weekly for 8 weeks | Implemented | No primaquine or tafenoquine without G6PD testing | Up to community level | Up to community malaria unit level | 2024 | Preferably administered under medical supervision, especially in areas with access to tertiary health care |
| **If no testing available** | No PQ or TQ | Implemented | No primaquine or tafenoquine without G6PD testing | Up to community level | Up to community malaria unit level | 2024 | _Not reported_ |
:::

### Country-specific policy context

<div class="country-policy-context">Brazil has approved the use of TQ in adults in 2023 with quant G6PD testing being rolled out being completed between June 2024 and April 2025 in 49 municipalities in six states and nine Special Indigenous Health Districts. In June 2025, Brazil adopted a child formulation of TQ.</div>
